notes: EBIT is proxied by “Income (loss) from operations” from the consolidated statements of operations. This includes impairment expense in 2025, so the base-case EBIT margin normalizes away from 2025 impairment dynamics rather than extrapolating it. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Capex is modeled from cash-flow line item “Additions to oil and natural gas properties” (cash basis proxy; excludes property acquisitions and other investing lines). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

NWC construction: NWC = (Total current assets − cash and cash equivalents) − (Total current liabilities − current maturities of debt), computed from year-end balance sheet line items. Negative NWC is retained as modeled. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Investments field left null because the balance sheet line separating investments (equity method investments vs. other assets) was not cleanly isolated in this research pass for a DCF plug with the requested schema granularity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

NOL utilization percent is an assumption (not directly disclosed as a utilization rate). NOL balance is taken from disclosed federal NOL amounts and the utilization rate is set conservatively for modeling. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

catalysts: Commodity-price driven re-rating of upstream earnings power and operating cash flows (oil/NGL price sensitivity). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Execution on the 2026 activity/capital plan (cash capital budget range) supporting production and free-cash-flow conversion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Any further impairment reversals or absence of future impairment charges could lift normalized EBIT margins relative to 2025. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))
company_overview: Independent oil and natural gas E&P focused primarily on the Permian Basin in West Texas, with revenue derived from oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids sales. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Reports under a consolidated upstream framework; key operating profitability is reflected in “Income (loss) from operations” and is materially impacted by non-cash items such as impairment. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Active capital program with 2026 cash capital budget guidance of approximately $3.60 billion to $3.90 billion (midpoint +~6% vs 2025). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))
current_context: FY2025 included total revenues of $15.026 billion and operating income of $1.266 billion, with “Depreciation, depletion, amortization and accretion” of $5.038 billion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Management’s latest disclosed 2026 capital budget range implies continued reinvestment discipline while preserving financial flexibility. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))
Current share price used for modeling is $192.54 (as provided by the market-data feed at the research timestamp).
investment_highlights: Base-case thesis assumes margin normalization after 2025’s impairment-driven EBIT volatility, with EBIT margin ramping toward ~0.38 by 2030 (using a reversion approach rather than extrapolating the 2025 impairment). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Capital intensity (capex as % of sales) is modeled to gradually decline from the elevated 2025 level, consistent with scale benefits and a steady-state reinvestment framework. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Negative net working capital contribution is retained in the base case (modeled NWC % of sales stays below zero), consistent with the company’s balance-sheet structure. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Tax and NOL assumptions reflect reported effective tax rate history and disclosed NOL carryforward/limitations framing. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Downside commodity cycles leading to lower revenues and pressured margins; impairments could re-emerge, distorting EBIT vs. normalized expectations. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Working-capital swings or timing of payable/receivable balances could change the NWC % of sales contribution materially vs. modeled levels. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Tax-rate volatility and limitations around loss utilization could reduce cash taxes vs. model or limit the benefit of NOLs. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1539838/000153983826000010/fang-20251231.htm))

Terminal value uses a Gordon-growth framework with economically reasonable long-run growth (2.0%) and a central WACC assumption (9.0%).
